# GEO report: Millstone Bakery

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 100/100, Strong

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100.

Every applicable rule is Clear, read from code. The site is plain static HTML, so there are no runtime values to be unsure about. The one thing code can't show is whether a CDN or firewall in front of the site blocks real crawlers.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

Nothing is wrong, so these are the biggest unknowns and the most useful additions.

### 1. Confirm real crawlers get through your host's protection
- **Why it matters:** A CDN or firewall can block crawlers even when `robots.txt` allows them, and code can't show that.
- **Where:** your access logs, not the repository
- **What the code says:** `robots.txt:1`: `User-agent: *` followed by `Allow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 100 whether it comes back clear or not. The code score doesn't cover the host.
- **How:** run `geopilot logs <access log file>`.

### 2. Run a live scan once the site is deployed
- **Why it matters:** It confirms the real status codes, redirects and headers that code can't prove.
- **Where:** the production URL
- **What the code says:** `sitemap.xml:3`: `<loc>https://www.millstonebakery.example/</loc>`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** the code score stays 100. The live score is calculated separately.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | `robots.txt` has valid lines and is tiny |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers can get in | Clear | `robots.txt:1-3`. Only `/members/` is blocked. GPTBot is blocked (`robots.txt:5-6`), which is a training-crawler choice and isn't counted. |
| GEO-014 | Key pages can be indexed | Clear | 4 of 4 routes. `members/index.html:9` has noindex and isn't in the sitemap. |
| GEO-015 | Canonical is absolute and on your domain | Clear | `index.html:8`, `breads.html:8`, `classes.html:8` |
| GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Clear | Static HTML pages |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is listed in robots | Clear | `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt:8` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and lang | Clear | All 4 pages |
| GEO-016 | Pages are reachable through real links | Clear | `<a href>` nav on every page |
| GEO-017 | Snippets are allowed | Clear | Only a scoped `data-nosnippet` at `breads.html:16`, which is a deliberate choice |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Read all 4 pages. `index.html:16` has alt text, and there are no other images or buttons. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not present. Not scored. |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not scored |

## Other problems found

None found.

## Worth considering

- **Label the bakery in structured data:** `index.html:6`: `<title>Millstone Bakery, sourdough in York</title>`. Nothing machine-readable states the name, address or hours. A `Bakery` (LocalBusiness) JSON-LD block on the home page with the name, address, opening hours and URL might help.
- **Say where the bakery is and when it's open:** `index.html:15`: `Pre-order for weekend collection.` The site never gives an address, hours or how to pre-order. Add them as text.
- **List the loaves:** `breads.html:15`: `Over twenty loaves through the week, including our seeded rye and the country white.` Only two are named. Listing all of them with days and prices backs up the claim. Each loaf could also get its own page.
- **Give the classes concrete details:** `classes.html:15`: `Book early, because places go quickly.` There are no dates, price, class size or booking route. Add them as text, and optionally as `Event` markup.
- **Link onward from the content:** `classes.html:15`. The Breads and Classes pages have no in-content links to each other or to ordering. Add a few.
- **Add `<lastmod>` dates:** `sitemap.xml:3`: `<url><loc>https://www.millstonebakery.example/</loc></url>`. Adding the real last-modified dates may help crawlers.
- **Add social tags:** `index.html:10`. There are no `og:title`, `og:description` or `og:image` tags, so shared links will look plain.
- **Make the page titles more specific:** `breads.html:6`: `Our breads | Millstone Bakery`. Adding "York" to the breads and classes titles, as the home page has, says where the bakery is.
- **Drop the redundant noindex-plus-block:** `robots.txt:3`: `Disallow: /members/`. Crawlers blocked by robots.txt never see the noindex at `members/index.html:9`. This is harmless, and it looks deliberate, so you can leave it.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live status codes and headers:** `X-Robots-Tag` headers and whether the sitemap URLs answer 200 need a live scan.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site. This matches `geo.config.json`, which has `aiSearchCrawlers: allow`.
- The `.example` domain is a placeholder for your real domain.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command if you want any of the ideas above applied. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
